scope: Complete Materials reconstruction through identity and traceability; crystals and quasicrystals; defects and microstructure; electronic and semiconductor organization; superconducting, superfluid and topological material response; mechanical, thermal, magnetic and optical response; bulk material classes; processing and degradation; and advanced functional and lifecycle organization.
exclusions: specimen- and method-dependent magnitudes are conditional records, not universal constants
biological function beyond the material interface belongs to Biology
clinical outcomes belong to Medicine and Health Sciences
industrial application performance cannot select a Materials law
unregistered materials and future observations remain new empirical targets

obligations.title: Material system and retained identity
obligations.statement: A material is the least complete constituent-and-relation carrier whose composition, bonding organization and declared observation boundary remain distinguishable.

obligations.title: Specimen and sampling relation
obligations.statement: A specimen is a source-bound finite part of a material with an explicit sampling map, retained preparation history and declared representativeness boundary.

obligations.title: Material composition record
obligations.statement: Material composition is the exact part-to-whole record of every retained component on one declared amount or support basis.

obligations.title: Material phase identity
obligations.statement: A material phase is a maximal connected support whose constituents share one stable recurrence and symmetry observation class at declared conditions.

obligations.title: Microstructure as mesoscale organization
obligations.statement: Microstructure is the complete declared-scale arrangement of phases, grains, interfaces and defects between constituent and bulk observation levels.

obligations.title: Material property relation
obligations.statement: A material property is a reproducible relation between a declared material state and stimulus/response records, conditional on direction, scale, history and method.

obligations.title: Materials uncertainty and metrological traceability
obligations.statement: A materials measurement is admissible only with a complete result, uncertainty, method, specimen, condition, calibration and unbroken reference chain.

obligations.title: Generated lattice organization
obligations.statement: A lattice is a completely generated site-and-adjacency network whose local word recurs under retained translations.

obligations.title: Primitive unit-cell identity
obligations.statement: A primitive unit cell is the least complete labelled cell whose generated translations reproduce every lattice site and relation once.

obligations.title: Crystalline translational order
obligations.statement: Crystalline translational order is invariance of the complete local constituent word and adjacency class under a generated integer translation basis.

obligations.title: Simple-cubic nearest-neighbour coordination
obligations.statement: Three stable spatial generators with two held orientations per generator force six nearest neighbours for the simple-cubic adjacency class.

obligations.title: Crystallographic rotation restriction
obligations.statement: A finite rotation preserves a periodic lattice only for generated orders 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6; five is the least excluded positive order.

obligations.title: Three-dimensional crystal-system classification
obligations.statement: Complete rank-three metric and crystallographic-rotation equivalence partitions periodic crystals into seven crystal-system classes.

obligations.title: Three-dimensional Bravais classification
obligations.statement: Complete rank-three translation lattices modulo basis and centering equivalence form fourteen Bravais classes.

obligations.title: Reciprocal support and diffraction
obligations.statement: Reciprocal support is the exact class of probe path labels whose phase returns coherently over the complete generated material organization; retained classes form diffraction peaks.

obligations.title: Quasicrystalline aperiodic order
obligations.statement: Quasicrystalline order is long-range coherent recurrence with sharp reciprocal support and no finite translation period; fivefold order is thereby admitted only outside periodic-lattice closure.

obligations.title: Acoustic lattice excitation branches
obligations.statement: A rank-three lattice has exactly one longitudinal and two transverse displacement orientations, forcing three acoustic excitation branches.

obligations.title: Point-defect identity
obligations.statement: A point defect is the least localized retained difference between an actual site record and its declared reference-lattice word.

obligations.title: Vacancy as structural absence
obligations.statement: A vacancy is a retained reference site carrying structural occupant absence, never deletion of the site or a numerical-zero material amount.

obligations.title: Interstitial and substitutional defects
obligations.statement: Interstitial and substitutional defects are distinguished respectively by an added occupied site relation and a changed occupant label at a retained reference site.

obligations.title: Dislocation line and slip
obligations.statement: A dislocation is a line-supported lattice mismatch whose complete circuit retains a nonclosing held translation and supplies a lawful slip path.

obligations.title: Grain and grain-boundary identity
obligations.statement: A grain is a maximal connected orientation-coherent crystal region; its boundary is the retained adjacency where two such orientation classes meet.

obligations.title: Material interface law
obligations.statement: A material interface is the complete boundary relation joining distinct material or phase carriers with explicit structural, content and transfer compatibility records.

obligations.title: Diffusive constituent transport
obligations.statement: Diffusion is counted adjacent-site redistribution of retained constituent labels with complete global content conservation and declared support/time recurrence.

obligations.title: Nucleation and phase growth
obligations.statement: A nucleus is the least generated cluster whose interior recurrence persists against its complete boundary relation; growth appends compatible cells while retaining phase and transfer provenance.

obligations.title: Electronic bands and structural gaps
obligations.statement: Electronic bands are complete phase-compatible recurrence classes on a material network; a band gap is a declared interval with no compatible generated state path.

obligations.title: Conductor, semiconductor and insulator distinction
obligations.statement: Conductor, semiconductor and insulator classes are forced by whether occupied carrier support connects to accessible states directly, across a finite activation gap, or not within the declared conditions.

obligations.title: Electron and hole carrier duality
obligations.statement: A binary exclusion-bounded state yields two transport descriptions: retained occupation and its held local absence, corresponding after sealing to electron and hole carriers.

obligations.title: Exclusion-bounded state occupation
obligations.statement: An exclusion-labelled canonical material mode admits structural absence or one retained indistinguishable occupation; a duplicate occupation is rejected.

obligations.title: Doping as controlled constituent substitution
obligations.statement: Doping is a source-bound substitution or addition that retains host organization while introducing an exact carrier-support difference.

obligations.title: p-type and n-type organization
obligations.statement: The two held orientations of a doped carrier imbalance force occupation-majority and absence-majority semiconductor classes.

obligations.title: p-n junction and depletion organization
obligations.statement: Joining opposed doped regions forces interfacial carrier transfer until a retained depletion/space-charge organization balances transport and field response at declared conditions.

obligations.title: Semiconductor transport relation
obligations.statement: Semiconductor transport is the complete counted motion of occupied and held-absence carriers through accessible support under declared field, gradient and scattering conditions.

obligations.title: Interband optical transition
obligations.statement: An interband optical response exists only when a probe supplies a complete compatible transition between retained occupied and accessible band states under the material selection rules.

obligations.title: Coherent paired-carrier state
obligations.statement: The least exclusion-compatible collective carrier joins two opposed fermionic labels into one integer-composite recurrence class.

obligations.title: Dissipation-closed superconducting transport
obligations.statement: Superconducting zero-resistance transport is phase-locked pair recurrence on complete connected support with no retained label-compatible dissipative transition.

obligations.title: Magnetic flux exclusion in the superconducting phase
obligations.statement: A phase-locked charged carrier network generates a boundary response whose complete bulk recurrence closes an incompatible applied magnetic distinction, yielding flux exclusion apart from the declared penetration boundary.

obligations.title: Superconducting flux quantization
obligations.statement: Single-valued return of a paired-carrier phase around a closed path forces whole winding classes and therefore discrete flux support.

obligations.title: Weak-link coherent transfer
obligations.statement: A weak link between phase-locked pair supports carries a coherent transfer recurrence determined by their retained phase distinction without dissolving pair identity.

obligations.title: Dissipation-closed superfluid transport
obligations.statement: Superfluid flow is shared-phase recurrence of a neutral collective carrier when the complete accessible transition census contains no allowed dissipative path below its first retained excitation boundary.

obligations.title: Quantized superfluid circulation
obligations.statement: Single-valued return of a superfluid phase around a closed path forces whole winding and discrete circulation classes with a retained vortex-core boundary.

obligations.title: Topological material invariant
obligations.statement: A material invariant is topological when its complete global path class is unchanged by every generated local deformation that retains connectivity and boundary records.

obligations.title: Bulk-boundary protected transport
obligations.statement: A nontrivial bulk path class forces a boundary recurrence whose removal would require closing the retained bulk distinction; compatible local backscattering paths are therefore absent within the declared gap.

obligations.title: Stress and strain records
obligations.statement: Stress is oriented load transfer per generated boundary support; strain is the exact retained change of internal separation relative to the same reference material state.

obligations.title: Elastic recovery
obligations.statement: Elastic response is a material transition path whose load release returns every retained constituent and adjacency relation to the original canonical state.

obligations.title: Plastic deformation
obligations.statement: Plastic response retains material content and phase identity while a defect-mediated transition changes the canonical adjacency organization after load release.

obligations.title: Dislocation-mediated slip
obligations.statement: Slip is a counted whole-lattice translation propagated by a retained dislocation along a compatible plane/direction without requiring simultaneous rupture of the complete plane.

obligations.title: Elastic modulus as response ratio
obligations.statement: An elastic modulus is the exact stress/strain response relation for one declared material direction, condition, reference state and reversible response window.

obligations.title: Strength and hardness boundaries
obligations.statement: Strength and hardness are method-bounded thresholds at which a declared loading path first produces retained plastic, indentation or failure organization.

obligations.title: Fracture and toughness
obligations.statement: Fracture is connected bond-path separation creating new retained boundary support; toughness is the declared resistance relation for crack initiation or advance with a complete work ledger.

obligations.title: Fatigue and creep
obligations.statement: Fatigue and creep are distinct history-dependent material processes: recurrence-counted damage under cyclic load and retained deformation under sustained load and time/temperature conditions.

obligations.title: Heat capacity and excitation storage
obligations.statement: Material heat capacity is the exact relation between supplied thermal carrier change and the resulting accessible excitation-support change at declared conditions.

obligations.title: Thermal conduction
obligations.statement: Thermal conduction is counted adjacent transfer of retained energy labels through connected material support with complete source, boundary and scattering provenance.

obligations.title: Thermal expansion
obligations.statement: Thermal expansion is the condition-bounded change of recurrent constituent separation with excitation while material identity and complete adjacency provenance remain retained.

obligations.title: Ferromagnetic order
obligations.statement: Ferromagnetism is connected recurrence of aligned local held-moment orientations producing a retained macroscopic orientation class.

obligations.title: Antiferromagnetic order
obligations.statement: Antiferromagnetism is stable opposed recurrence on distinguishable sublattices that retains local order while the complete macroscopic moment distinction closes.

obligations.title: Dielectric polarization
obligations.statement: Dielectric polarization is a retained field-conditioned redistribution or orientation of bound held-charge labels with complete conservation and relaxation records.

obligations.title: Optical propagation and refractive response
obligations.statement: Material refractive response is the source-bound phase/delay relation produced by coherent probe coupling to accessible material excitations while propagation, loss and dispersion records remain separate.

obligations.title: Material phase transition
obligations.statement: A material phase transition is a provenance-retaining change between stable macro-recurrence and symmetry classes with explicit conditions, path and hysteresis boundary.

obligations.title: Metallic material organization
obligations.statement: A metallic material is a connected atomic organization with delocalized carrier access across multiple constituent cells and no declared transport gap at its operating conditions.

obligations.title: Ceramic material organization
obligations.statement: A ceramic is an inorganic nonmetallic material whose bulk carrier is a localized ionic/covalent network with retained phase, porosity and grain/interface organization.

obligations.title: Polymeric material organization
obligations.statement: A polymeric material is a population of covalently recurrent chain carriers with explicit repeat identity, sequence, length/branching distribution and interchain organization.

obligations.title: Composite material organization
obligations.statement: A composite is a joint material whose distinguishable constituent carriers persist while interfaces and architecture compose their load, transport or barrier responses.

obligations.title: Glass and amorphous organization
obligations.statement: A glass is a connected material with retained local structural recurrence but no crystalline translation class, whose macrostate depends on preparation and observation-time relaxation.

obligations.title: Porous material organization
obligations.statement: A porous material is a joint solid/structural-absence support whose pore connectivity, interface and accessibility are retained at a declared resolution.

obligations.title: Molecular-to-bulk correspondence
obligations.statement: A bulk material law is admitted only when the complete constituent/interaction network composes to a scale-stable observation while fluctuations, interfaces and preparation history remain explicitly bounded.

obligations.title: Material anisotropy
obligations.statement: Anisotropy is inequality of response relations across retained material directions after specimen, condition and method identities are held fixed.

obligations.title: Size and surface effects
obligations.statement: A material size effect occurs when the exact boundary/interior support relation changes the accessible state, transfer or mechanical census; it is never a free scale correction.

obligations.title: Processing–structure–property path
obligations.statement: A materials process is a complete ordered path from input carrier through retained structural states to property relations; endpoint labels alone cannot erase the path.

obligations.title: Phase stability and coexistence organization
obligations.statement: A phase map partitions generated composition/condition support by the stable material recurrence class, retaining coexistence, fraction and transition boundaries without fitted extrapolation beyond its domain.

obligations.title: Solidification
obligations.statement: Solidification is the ordered nucleation and growth path from mobile to position-retaining organization with complete energy, constituent rejection and interface provenance.

obligations.title: Sintering and densification
obligations.statement: Sintering is interface-mediated constituent transport that joins particles and reorganizes structural absence while conserving material content and retaining the processing path.

obligations.title: Heat treatment
obligations.statement: Heat treatment is a declared thermal/time path whose phase, defect and microstructure transitions are retained and whose property consequence is path-bound.

obligations.title: Corrosion
obligations.statement: Corrosion is an interfacial reaction/transport process that transforms a material and environment jointly while retaining complete constituent, charge, product and boundary provenance.

obligations.title: Wear and tribological material transfer
obligations.statement: Wear is retained material transfer or surface reorganization produced by a declared contact/load/motion path; frictional response and material loss remain separately recorded.

obligations.title: Radiation damage
obligations.statement: Radiation damage is the complete source-bound path from probe energy transfer to retained displacement, excitation or transmutation defects and their subsequent migration/recovery.

obligations.title: Piezoelectric coupling
obligations.statement: Piezoelectricity is a reversible cross-relation between mechanical deformation and held electric polarization permitted only when the retained material symmetry does not close the orientation distinction.

obligations.title: Ferroelectric order and switching
obligations.statement: Ferroelectricity is a material phase with stable opposed polarization recurrence classes and a retained field-driven switching path between them.

obligations.title: Thermoelectric coupling
obligations.statement: Thermoelectric response is the joint conserved relation between energy-gradient transport and held-charge transport on the same material network.

obligations.title: Photonic material organization
obligations.statement: A photonic material organizes electromagnetic recurrence support so that allowed propagation classes and structural gaps follow from complete generated geometry and boundary relations.

obligations.title: Functional magnetic material response
obligations.statement: A functional magnetic response is the complete relation among applied field, domain transition path, retained orientation, loss and remanence at declared frequency and temperature.

obligations.title: Nanoscale material boundary
obligations.statement: A nanomaterial regime begins when boundary and finite-support distinctions remain in the material state/property census and cannot be closed by the bulk observation quotient.

obligations.title: Biomaterial interface boundary
obligations.statement: A biomaterial claim is a joint material/biological interface relation with explicit exposure, transfer, response and function boundaries; biological outcomes cannot select the material law.

obligations.title: Material lifecycle and recyclability
obligations.statement: A material lifecycle is the complete source-to-processing-to-use-to-recovery flow ledger; recyclability requires an explicit identity-preserving recovery path and records every transformation, loss and quality boundary.

obligations.title: Exact quasicrystal substitution inflation
obligations.statement: The two-label substitution A to AB and B to A generates an exact positive finite successor chain whose population pair never admits a positive rational fixed scale satisfying the recurrence.

obligations.title: Acoustic, optical and thermal mode limits
obligations.statement: Uniform shared displacement supplies a gapless acoustic class, a retained two-constituent basis supplies an opposed optical class, and positive rank-three support contains the exact cube count of low-support modes and three displacement modes per site at complete support.

obligations.title: Exact p-n junction rectification
obligations.statement: The two held bias orientations of a retained p-n junction force distinct forward barrier-opening and reverse barrier-strengthening transition classes without signed proof quantities.

obligations.title: Superconducting isotope-response record
obligations.statement: A superconducting isotope comparison is admissible only when isotope identity, constituent-mass distinction and transition response are retained together while the observation remains incapable of selecting the pairing law.

obligations.title: Ferrimagnetic sublattice order
obligations.statement: Opposed distinguishable magnetic sublattices with unequal positive counted moment support force a nonempty partial bulk moment class distinct from aligned and equal-opposed order.

obligations.title: Integer and primary fractional Hall classes
obligations.statement: A gapped oriented two-generator material carrier retains whole winding classes and a separately bounded primary hierarchy of reduced positive odd-denominator parts, invariant under gap-preserving deformation.

obligations.title: Exact topological boundary-mode count
obligations.statement: For two distinct adjacent whole bulk winding classes, the exact protected boundary recurrence count is their positive whole gap with orientation retained as a label rather than a signed number.

obligations.title: Hydrogen-bonded water bulk-response ledger
obligations.statement: A water bulk-response claim must retain the molecular hydrogen-bond network, specimen and phase identity, boiling, solid/liquid density and heat-capacity observations with their conditions, methods and uncertainty boundaries.
